Technical Architecture & Privacy Model

Unlike conventional online utilities that transmit sensitive files or payloads to remote cloud servers, UtilForge processes data entirely inside your browser's isolated local memory. Whether you are formatting proprietary customer records, confidential database queries, API credentials, or internal schemas, your payload is never sent over any network socket.

By leveraging native browser standards—including the Web Cryptography API (SubtleCrypto), HTML5 Canvas, and native JavaScript V8 parsing engines—transformations execute with sub-millisecond latency while maintaining an airtight zero-retention privacy boundary. This ensures full architectural compatibility with strict corporate compliance standards, including SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR data-isolation requirements.

Frequently Asked Questions (Unix Timestamp Converter)

How can I tell if a timestamp is in seconds or milliseconds?

Current Unix timestamps in seconds are 10 digits long (e.g., 1792236447), whereas millisecond timestamps are 13 digits long (e.g., 1792236447000).
